newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT/Retail game seen as survival of fittest.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT/Retail game seen as survival of fittest.

text.p: Despite a competitive environment with many retailers still limping from the recession in the early 1990s, analysts say the most dominant chains will continue to grab market share and boost earnings as the economy remains strong.

"There is going to be a big blowout in consumer demand," said Otto Grote, a sell side analyst that heads Derby Securities. "Retail sector stocks are an indicator with what is happening in the economy."
This should lead to higher earnings and higher values for retail stocks, despite a recent slump in U.S. stocks over interest rate fears, Grote said.

John Hughes, a retailing analyst at Piper Jaffray, said investors have to be selective about what retailers they choose, however. Regardless of the economic climate, Hughes said there is an "over-stored and over-cataloged environment."

William Armstrong, an analyst at Fahnestock & Co, said investors really need to be selective about retailers, since the low inflation environment and abundance of stores makes it difficult for retailers to raise prices.
People will continue to be price sensitive, despite the healthy economy because of high personal debt levels, said John Hughes, an analyst at Piper Jaffray.

Retailers have had a good run for the first three months of the year, judging by the Standard & Poor's Retail Index. Mediocre same-store sales for the holidays helped push the index to a 1997 low of 360.45 on January 28.
Good profit growth for the period ended January pushed retail stocks higher, with the index reaching a high of 481.71 on March 19.
Retailers in the index continued to gain after the Dow Jones industrial average hit an all-time high of 7158.28 on March 11, but the indices lately have moved in tandem.
Grote is recommending that investors buy large-cap retail stocks that specialize in hard goods, including Wal-Mart Stores Inc and Dollar General Corp, over apparel retailers.
Similar traits in the retailers he picks include concepts driven by "merchant-artists" and strong management.
Armstrong has buy recommendations on Kmart Corp, Federated Department Stores Inc and Sports Authority.

In the discount retail segment, size really counts since the regional discounters are suffering while Dayton Hudson Corp's Target, Wal-Mart Stores Inc and Kmart Corp can offer lower prices, Armstrong said.

Grote prefers "baskets" of retail stocks rather than a select few. The strategy offers similar benefits to a mutual fund by spreading risk and increasing your chances of landing winning stocks, he said.
Grote said there are typically two rallies for retailing stocks during an economic expansion, forming the Retail Sector Stock Cycle.

The first comes immediately after the first signs of economic recovery after a recession. "In that part of an upturn, you can't make money except as a trader. You have a period of underperformance after the first uptick."
The second comes when economic growth is starting to peak.
The time to sell comes when there are the first signs of a slowdown. "Only three percent of retailers do well during downturns," Grote said. "These are cyclical growth stocks."
Investors, however, are "continuously behind this cycle," Grote said. "Wall Street has always had the mistaken concept that retailers are early business cycle stocks."
